{{Wireless adapter |brand=Philips |model=PTA01 |revision=/00 |asin=B003CXT2W4 |fcc_date=05/13/2010 |manuf_country=China |is_manuf=No |manuf=Alpha Networks |manuf_model=WUS-N11 |if=USB |if_bus_version=2.0 |if_connector_type=Male A |form_factor=dongle |vendor_id=0471 |device_id=209e |fcc_id=BOUWUB1110 |chip1_brand=Atheros |chip1_model=AR9271 |accessible_UART=No |ant_conn=U.FL |802dot11_protocols=bgn |txchains=1 |rxchains=1 |sstreams=1 |oui=5C:33:8E |lin_driver= |win_driver= }} '''PTA01/00 - TV Wireless Network USB Adapter''' This device is used with some Philips TVs. :CMIIT ID: 2010DJ1591 :Anatel: 0865-10-6021 [http://forum.wdlxtv.com/viewtopic.php?f=31&t=4713 ID mention] The device USB ID was added to Linux kernel version 4.1, :but the chipset is supported since kernel v2.6.35. For kernel versions earlier than v4.1, you can add the ID manually: 
modprobe ath9k_htc
echo 0471 209e > /sys/bus/usb/drivers/ath9k_htc/new_id
To add the ID permanently, see: [http://pastebin.com/aAu9bRzP Easy tutorial on setting up pta01/00 on linux (Linux driver)] You can use your PTA-01 on Windows. Inside, there is Atheros AR9271. :You can find it here: [https://www.atheros-drivers.com/download-driver-for-Atheros-chipset-with-id-64-and-Windows7-64bit.html Windows 7 (64bit) driver] Just manually install driver, and if ask that it's not correct driver, say Yes. This is a picture of an opened stick: [http://upload.slike.com/slike/ETNr.jpg image] :From the picture, it appears to be a [[Philips WUB1110]]. :The FCC ID of the WUB1110 (BOUWUB1110) has been assigned to it.
